one_liner: Deterministic reactor language whose generated C++ (reactor-cpp runtime) ran the ported Savina suite faster than CAF and Akka.
what_it_does: Lingua Franca (LF) is a coordination language: you declare reactors, ports, logical actions and static connections in .lf files, write reaction bodies in a target language (here C++), and the lfc code generator emits a CMake project linked against the reactor-cpp runtime. It is not a drop-in actor library: Savina programs were rewritten as fixed reactor graphs with logical-time semantics, and the benchmark harness (lf-lang/benchmarks-lingua-franca runner/) builds and runs each port next to the CAF and Akka versions from the lf-lang/savina fork.
how_it_is_fast: reactor-cpp schedules reactions of a statically known dependency graph on a worker pool, tag by tag: reactions at the same logical tag that are not ordered by the graph run in parallel, and no per-message mailbox or dynamic actor creation is needed. Fan-out goes through connections rather than messages: in the Fork Join throughput port one set() on a void output broadcast via (producer.outMessage)+ triggers all 60 worker reactions, where CAF enqueues 600,000 individual message_t objects into 60 mailboxes. Benchmarks build with build-type Release and no-runtime-validation (runtime checks compiled out), and PingPong adds fast: true.
when_to_use: New concurrent C++ code with a fixed set of components and connections where reproducible, deterministic behaviour (testable, replayable) matters as much as throughput.
Pipelines and fan-out/fan-in workloads that map onto a static reactor graph, where broadcast connections replace per-receiver message copies.
Embedded or cyber-physical systems that need explicit logical timing alongside multicore execution (the C target and reactor-uc cover small devices).
Teams willing to adopt the lfc toolchain (Java-based code generator) and write reaction bodies inside .lf files.
when_not_to_use: Workloads that create actors dynamically (Fibonacci, Quicksort, Fork Join create): the snippet-reported paper results cover only the benchmarks expressible as static graphs, and LF reactor graphs are fixed at startup apart from the unfinished mutations work (reactor-cpp issue #61, open).
Latency-bound two-party message exchange: the paper (snippet) reports LF behind CAF on Ping Pong and Thread Ring.

Long-lived production C++ services: reactor-cpp, the C++ runtime behind these numbers, has carried a 'currently not actively maintained' banner since 2025-05-20 (contributors moved to the Xronos SDK fork and reactor-uc).
Existing CAF or Akka code bases: there is no migration path; every actor must be rewritten as a reactor with declared ports.
Distributed actor systems that rely on location transparency or supervision trees; LF federations are a different model.

integration.form: code generator (lfc) emitting a CMake project linked against the reactor-cpp static library
integration.dependencies: lfc (Java toolchain), CMake, reactor-cpp runtime (fetched by the generated build); the comparison harness needs Python with hydra-core, cogapp and pandas, CAF 0.16.5 and a Java 8 JDK for Savina/Akka
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 (reactor-cpp CMakeLists sets CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17; its 'Update to C++20' issue #35 was closed on 2025-05-20 with the standard still 17); compiler versions used in the paper not documented
integration.platforms: Not documented on the pages opened (the benchmark runner's printSystemInfo has Windows, macOS, Linux and BSD branches, but that only prints the OS name); paper hardware not confirmed
integration.thread_safety: Deterministic by construction: reactions of one reactor never run concurrently and state is reactor-local; the runtime owns the worker pool (--workers). reactor-cpp issue #34 (sync_shutdown not thread safe) was fixed in 2022.

gotchas: Harness asymmetry in the public code: the CAF timed region is run_iteration(), which constructs and destroys a whole caf::actor_system (spawning and joining the scheduler's max-threads workers) and spawns every actor; the Akka timed region likewise creates a new ActorSystem per iteration and awaits its termination. The LF BenchmarkRunner starts its clock at start.set() with the reactor graph and worker pool already built, so system startup and teardown are charged to the baselines only; the size of this bias was not measured.

CAF iteration times are truncated to whole milliseconds (duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds> before conversion to double) while LF reports fractional milliseconds; the runner's parser takes both at face value.

Ports are not line-for-line: Fork Join throughput becomes one void broadcast per round to 60 workers instead of 600,000 mailbox messages from the main thread, and PingPong breaks its causality loop with a logical action, so wins partly reflect the reactor model avoiding message traffic the actor versions must perform.

Build defaults differ: LF ports use CMake Release (-O3 -DNDEBUG) with runtime validation off, while lf-lang/savina's CMakeLists defaults CAF programs to RelWithDebInfo (-O2 -g -fno-omit-frame-pointer); the runner's lf-cpp target also builds against reactor-cpp runtime_version 'master', so a rerun today does not use the paper's runtime revision.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick LF over the Pony actor entries when you want C++ reaction code and deterministic, testable concurrency on a static component graph; Pony (and CAF itself) fit better when actors are created dynamically or message order nondeterminism is acceptable. Against Tokio or goroutine entries it is a different model (logical-time reactors, not async tasks) and only makes sense if determinism is a requirement.
verified_claims_summary: Per web-search snippets of the ACM TACO 2023 paper (not opened here; arXiv, cfaed.tu-dresden.de and fis.tu-dresden.de unreachable), LF's C++ target averaged about 1.42x faster than CAF and 1.86x faster than Akka over the Savina benchmarks it could port, losing to CAF on Ping Pong and Thread Ring. The public harness pins Akka 2.6.17 (lf-lang/savina pom.xml) and CAF 0.16.5 (benchmark README), but CPU, compiler, thread count and aggregation could not be confirmed, and the baselines' timed regions include actor-system startup and teardown that LF's do not.
status_note: Lingua Franca itself is active (BSD-2-Clause, commits through 2026-09) and the benchmark repo was touched on 2026-09-20, but the C++ runtime that produced these numbers, reactor-cpp, has been marked unmaintained since 2025-05-20, so treat the C++ target as a research artifact rather than a supported product.
